title: Downhill all the way: which valley?
hook: A ball always steps downhill. Does it always find the lowest point?

knows: that gradient descent takes small steps downhill on a loss curve
doesNotKnow: that the starting point can decide which valley descent settles in
that descent cannot climb out of a shallow valley to reach a deeper one

misconception: Rolling downhill always reaches the lowest point.
objective: The learner can say that small downhill steps stop in the valley on the starting side of a hump, so descent finds the nearest valley, not necessarily the lowest.

claims.text: The curve f(x) = x⁴ − 3x² + x and the step rule (step size 0.01, 2000 steps) are a toy, labelled 'Toy curve · small downhill steps' on the stage.
claims.source: Brief 47 in company/domains/briefs/ai.md; MODEL block in Demo.tsx.

claims.text: Released at x = 1.5 or 0.5, the ball stops at x = 1.13 (height −1.07); released at x = −0.5 or −1.5, it reaches x = −1.30 (height −3.51), the deeper valley.
The hump between the valleys is near x = 0.17, where the slope 4x³ − 6x + 1 is zero; starts on either side of it end in different valleys.
claims.source: HUMP in Demo.tsx (bisection on [0, 0.5]): 0.1699. node: start 0.2 → 1.131, start 0.15 → −1.301.

claims.text: Gradient descent in real model training follows the same downhill rule, so its starting point can affect where it ends.
claims.source: About real systems: Goodfellow, Bengio & Courville 2016, Deep Learning, §8.2.2 (local minima) and §8.4 (initialisation affects the outcome). Do not overclaim: for large networks many local minima found have similar loss (Choromanska et al. 2015; Dauphin et al. 2014); the lesson does not say real training usually gets stuck.

recall.question: Two runs of the same descent on the same curve start on opposite sides of a hump. What should you expect?
options: Both reach the lowest point eventually
They may settle in different valleys, because each step only goes downhill from where it is
Both stop on top of the hump
recall.why: Downhill steps cannot climb a hump, so each run settles in the valley on its own side. The nearest valley need not be the lowest.
